doc.avatar_a11y_spec: Prevent information duplication or confusion by properly setting the alt attribute to the username if there is an image, or aria-hidden="true" for decorative purposes.
doc.avatar_anatomy_badge: An indicator for showing login status (online/offline) or that there are unread notifications (optional).
doc.avatar_anatomy_visual: Displays a profile image, initials, or a default icon.
doc.avatar_best_practice_1: Always provide a meaningful fallback (initials or icon) for when the image fails to load.
doc.avatar_best_practice_2: Use consistent sizing across similar contexts (e.g., all avatars in a comment section should be the same size).
doc.avatar_choice_avatar_when: When you want to display specific users or brands and emphasize their individuality by linking them with names.
doc.avatar_choice_icon_when: When you want to independently represent functions or categories that do not have a specific personality (such as 'Settings' or 'Home').
doc.avatar_choice_image_when: When you want to display the content itself (such as product photos) rather than the user themselves.
doc.avatar_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the type of information to be displayed and ease of identification.
doc.avatar_colors_desc: Specify background colors for initials or icons.
doc.avatar_content_guidelines: Layer fallbacks so that initials are displayed if there is no image, and a generic silhouette icon is displayed if initials are also unknown.
doc.avatar_design_intent: Avatar provides a visual clue for identifying users or entities at a glance. By including images or initials in addition to presenting names in text, it makes the interface more human and friendly.
doc.avatar_fallback_desc: Displays initials or icons when the image URL is invalid or missing.
doc.avatar_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the alt and aria-label props.
doc.avatar_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction beyond standard Tab focus.
doc.avatar_long_desc: A component for displaying user profile images, initials, or icons in circular or rectangular shapes. Includes built-in fallback display for missing or failed image loads.
doc.avatar_motion_spec: When functioning as a link, communicate that it is clickable by slightly increasing the size or changing the brightness on hover.
doc.avatar_scenario_chat: Chat List: Displays a combination of the other's image and online status (badge).

doc.avatargroup_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction beyond standard Tab focus.
doc.badge_best_practice_1: Keep badge text short and concise so the meaning is conveyed at a glance.

doc.card_a11y_spec: When making the entire card a link, consider the order in which screen readers read and explore structures (such as focus on headings) to avoid redundant reading.

doc.card_guideline_2: Ideal for displaying multiple independent contents, such as dashboard summaries or product listings.

doc.patterns_error_desc: An UX-friendly error screen pattern combining `Center`, `Stack`, `Heading`, `Paragraph`, `Alert`, and `Button`.
doc.patterns_hero_desc: A pattern for an eye-catching main visual used on the top page of a website, etc. It combines `Grid`, `Stack`, `Heading`, `Paragraph`, `Button`, `Avatar`, and others.

doc.patterns_login_desc: A standard login form pattern combining `Card`, `Input`, `Button`, `Stack`, and others. It includes examples of validation and social login button placement.
doc.patterns_motion_desc: Transitions are minimal and purposeful, respecting the user's reduced-motion preferences.
doc.patterns_pricing_desc: A common pricing comparison table pattern for SaaS, etc. It uses `Grid`, `Card`, `Badge`, `Heading`, `Paragraph`, `Button`, and `Stack` for a layout with clear information priority.
doc.patterns_profile_desc: A settings screen pattern combining many form components like `Input`, `Textarea`, `Selectbox`, `RadioGroup`, and `Switch`. It features a two-column layout with a sidebar navigation and a main content area.
doc.patterns_scenario_1: Dashboard Layouts: Rapidly assembling a main view using pre-composed card and grid patterns.
doc.patterns_scenario_2: Marketing Pages: Implementing high-impact hero sections and pricing tables with minimal custom CSS.

doc.virtuallist_a11y_desc: Uses role="list" and role="listitem" with aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex attributes to inform assistive technologies about the total number of items and current position.
doc.virtuallist_anatomy_inner: A full-height container that establishes the scrollable height matching the total items count.
doc.virtuallist_anatomy_item: A fixed-height wrapper for each rendered item, positioned via CSS transform.
doc.virtuallist_anatomy_root: The scrollable outer container with a fixed display height.
doc.virtuallist_best_practice_1: Always provide a fixed itemHeight that matches the actual rendered height of each item to prevent layout misalignment.
doc.virtuallist_best_practice_2: Use the overscan prop to reduce visual flickering during fast scrolling — a value between 3 and 10 is recommended.
doc.virtuallist_best_practice_3: For items with varying heights, consider using a layout that normalizes item height or use a dedicated dynamic-height virtualization solution.
doc.virtuallist_best_practice_4: VirtualList and InfiniteScroll solve different problems and work well together — use InfiniteScroll to fetch data incrementally and VirtualList to keep rendering lightweight as items accumulate.
doc.virtuallist_choice_alt_infinite_when: When data is fetched incrementally from a server on scroll. Can be combined with VirtualList when the accumulated items grow large.
doc.virtuallist_choice_alt_list_when: When the total number of items is small (under ~100) and full DOM rendering is acceptable.
doc.virtuallist_choice_alt_table_when: When items need to be displayed in a tabular format with column headers and sorting.
doc.virtuallist_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.virtuallist_choice_self_when: When rendering large datasets (hundreds to tens of thousands of items) where full DOM rendering would degrade performance.
doc.virtuallist_content_guideline_1: Keep renderItem output lightweight — avoid heavy computations or deeply nested components inside each item.
doc.virtuallist_content_guideline_2: Ensure each item has a consistent visual height matching the itemHeight prop.
doc.virtuallist_custom_height_desc: Set itemHeight to match the actual height of your item content.
doc.virtuallist_desc: Efficiently renders large lists by virtualizing off-screen items
doc.virtuallist_design_intent: VirtualList provides a performant rendering strategy for large datasets by only mounting items currently visible in the viewport. This dramatically reduces DOM size and memory usage compared to rendering all items at once.
doc.virtuallist_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through each item's content.
doc.virtuallist_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys navigate between list items. Tab moves focus to each interactive item. Enter or Space activates the focused item.
doc.virtuallist_large_dataset_desc: Even with 10,000 items, only a small subset is rendered in the DOM at any time.
doc.virtuallist_long_desc: A virtualized list component that efficiently handles large datasets by rendering only visible items.
doc.virtuallist_motion_desc: Items are repositioned via CSS transform for smooth, GPU-accelerated scrolling without layout recalculation.
doc.virtuallist_overscan_desc: The overscan prop controls how many extra items are rendered outside the visible area to reduce flickering during fast scrolling.
doc.virtuallist_scenario_1: Infinite Scrolling Logs: Handling tens of thousands of system log entries without memory degradation.
doc.virtuallist_scenario_2: Product Catalogs: Rendering extensive e-commerce listings while maintaining smooth scrolling performance.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_desc: You can use Chrome DevTools to verify how content in the `VisuallyHidden` component is recognized by screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_step_1_desc: Right-click on the part where `VisuallyHidden` is used in the browser and select "Inspect" to open DevTools.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_step_2_desc: Click the "Switch to Accessibility Tree view" button (person-shaped icon) at the top right of the `Elements` panel. This switches the DOM tree to a representation interpreted by screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_a11y_step_3_desc: Select the target element from the tree. In the `Accessibility` tab (select from `>>` if not visible) on the right, the content displayed as `Name: "..."` in the `Computed Properties` section is the text that will actually be read aloud.
doc.visuallyhidden_case_button_desc: Used when a text label is needed for something visually understood, like an icon-only button.
doc.visuallyhidden_desc: Hide content visually while keeping it accessible to screen readers
doc.visuallyhidden_i18n_desc: All visible text uses i18n keys. Pass translated strings through the children prop.
doc.visuallyhidden_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. It hides content visually while keeping it accessible to screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_long_desc: `VisuallyHidden` is a utility component used when you want to hide content visually while still conveying that information to assistive technologies like screen readers.
doc.visuallyhidden_usage_desc: Content wrapped in this component will not be displayed on the screen but will still exist in the HTML structure.
